newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hails resumption of financial services talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hails resumption of financial services talks.

text.p: The United States welcomed the resumption of negotiations on financial services under the World Trade Organisation on Monday, saying it was committed to non-discriminatory free market access.

In a joint statement by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, the United States said its financial markets were the most open in the world and that other countries should follow suit.

"If our trading partners want legal guarantees in the WTO that the United States will not restrict access to its financial services market, then they must work with us to ensure that each WTO member with substantial markets provides similar guarantees," the statement said.
"This ambitious undertaking will require a higher standard of liberalisation than has been offered to date by a number of key emerging markets," it added.
Meeting in Geneva, representatives from major powers and emerging economies began a round of talks aimed at shaping a global pact by the end of the year to open up markets for financial services.

Before the discussions got under way, a U.S. official in Geneva said that Washington, which stood aloof from an interim deal involving 43 countries two years ago, was committed to try to make the negotiations a success.
Participation by the United States is seen as vital for a meaningful agreement, which would come under the umbrella of the WTO and its book of rules.
In its statement, the United States said it expected recent successes in WTO negotiations on telecommunications and services to establish a firm basis for moving forward in financial services.

"Our objective in the negotiations is commitments from our trading partners to provide substantially full market access and national treatment to our companies," the statement said. "In return, we are prepared to commit ourselves to do the same."
